newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices mostly hold steady again.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices mostly hold steady again.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices, helped by firmer crude, mostly were unchanged again Wednesday in quiet trade, but mild weather and cheap gas prices kept underlying sentiment more bearish, industry sources said.

"Utilities aren't burning much, but any burn is more likely to be gas than fuel. The tone is pretty bearish," said one cash trader, adding a number of East Coast utilities recently switched from resid to cheaper natgas.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent held steady at about $16.25-50 a barrel, with March one percent paper sold at $16.35, down slightly from Tuesday despite the crude gain.
NYH April one percent paper slipped slightly to about $16.25, while Q2 was also quoted at about $16.25.

NYH 0.3 percent high pour seemed to stabilize at the $17.25 area, helped by reports of a 50,000-barrel HP sale at a published high plus 65 cents (delivered Mass). But traders said city gate gas prices hovering just under $14 a barrel equivalent were likely to keep the grade on the defensive.
NYH high sulphurs also were unchanged, with three percent still pegged near $15.

At the U.S. Gulf, one percent again held steady at about $15.25, while three percent climbed 25-50 cents to $13.00-25 on reports a major sold 40,000 barrels of 2.6-2.8 percent at $13.90 (FOB Port Arthur, Texas).
New York city gate gas prices were unchanged at about $2.15-20/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid still at a $2.60/mmBtu equivalent.
